title: Playing for low pay in Decatur Street joints in the 1930s
summary: George recalls working for six bits and a dollar a night at the Kingfish, Mama's Place and others, and who played with him.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Did you ever work for really low prices?
I worked for low prices right in the thirties there.

I worked for one job, I was just talking to my mother right there. Decatur, not my son, he's bringing me over here. Decatur, Toulouse, Decatur. And then there's a little Shaw Street coming from St. Peter. Wilkinson. Wilkinson. They had a saloon right on that corner. And I worked there one night from eight until four in the morning for six bits.
Which corner was it? Downtown or the uptown?
On the downtown and the uptown side of Bangor, there was a giant right there.
On the downtown? On the lake side. Downtown and the lake side?
On the back of town side, what you call the back of town, and the uptown side. Uptown.
Yeah. That's torn down there. Yeah, it's torn down. A big block.
Little shop right next to that shop. Been there for years. A loading shop. Been there for many, many years.
Yeah, that's right. The same block that I live in. That's right.
And then I worked at the kingfish for two years or something. For a dollar a night. And I never missed a night. Where was the kingfish? Oystin Island and Decatur. Where they sell chickens.

Then I moved from there and I went in the middle of the block to another little place. It was called Mama's Place. And I got a dollar a night there. And I moved further down the block to the Popeye and got a dollar a night there.
Was that every night or just on weekends? Every night. Every night.

Who was playing with you in some of those jumps? Well, the first one I was at Kingfish was Boyd's. Boyd's was playing trumpet. Boyd's Stevens was playing trumpet. Boyd's. And the guy by the name of McGee was playing drum. And Billy, Billy Chase was playing piano. He was on the four of us.
Now McGee, is that, that's Herb Moran?

No, that's not Herb Moran's brother. That's another McGee. That's another McGee. Yeah, he lives in Oakland right now. He was one of the last time I saw him. He quit playing. Used to wear a derby all the time. And then after Boyd's left there, that's where the D came in there. That's where him and Billy got acquainted and got married for. I stood for the wait.
